# dstevx

> Computes the eigenvalues and, optionally, the left and/or right eigenvectors.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dstevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dstevx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dstevx(
    order,
    jobz, range,
    N,
    d, strideD,
    e, strideE,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    M,
    w, strideW,
    Z, LDZ,
    WORK,
    IWORK,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'`: Compute eigenvalues only; `'compute-vectors'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors. |
| `range` | `"all" \| "value" \| "index"` | `'all'`: all eigenvalues will be found. `'value'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (VL,VU] will be found. `'index'`: the IL-th through IU-th eigenvalues will be found. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix A. On exit, D may be multiplied by a constant factor chosen to avoid over/underflow in computing the eigenvalues. |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length max(1, N - 1)</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the (n-1) subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix A in elements 1 to N-1 of E. On exit, E may be multiplied by a constant factor chosen to avoid over/underflow in computing the eigenvalues. |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| `vl` | `number` | If `range === 'value'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. |
| `vu` | `number` | If `range === 'value'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues.<br>Rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` |
| `il` | `integer` | If `range === 'index'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. 1 <= IL <= IU <= N, if N > 0.<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max(1, N))` |
| `iu` | `integer` | If `range === 'index'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. 1 <= IL <= IU <= N, if N > 0.<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min(N, il) \|\| iu > N)` |
| `abstol` | `number` | The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | **out** · The total number of eigenvalues found. 0 <= M <= N. |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · The first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order. |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)</sub> | **out** · If `jobz === 'compute-vectors'`, then if INFO = 0, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with W(i). |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Z`<br>Rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `5 * N` elements |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `5 * N` elements |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · If `jobz === 'compute-vectors'`, then if INFO = 0, the first M elements of IFAIL are zero (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | Stride length for `IFAIL` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found.
  -   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found.
  -   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found.
- `N`: The order of the matrix. $N \ge 0$.
- `d`: On entry, the n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix A. On exit, D may be multiplied by a constant factor chosen to avoid over/underflow in computing the eigenvalues.
- `e`: On entry, the (n-1) subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix A in elements 1 to N-1 of E. On exit, E may be multiplied by a constant factor chosen to avoid over/underflow in computing the eigenvalues.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.

  See "Computing Small Singular Values of Bidiagonal Matrices with Guaranteed High Relative Accuracy," by Demmel and Kahan, LAPACK Working Note #3.
- `M`: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.
- `w`: The first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. If an eigenvector fails to converge (`INFO` \> 0), then that column of Z contains the latest approximation to the eigenvector, and the index of the eigenvector is returned in `IFAIL`. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced. Note: the user must ensure that at least max(1,M) columns are supplied in the array Z; if `RANGE = 'V'`, the exact value of M is not known in advance and an upper bound must be used.
- `IFAIL`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M elements of `IFAIL` are zero. If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, then `IFAIL` contains the indices of the eigenvectors that failed to converge. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then `IFAIL` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < max( 1, range === "index" ? iu - il + 1 : N ) )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dstevx.ndarray(
    jobz, range,
    N,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    e, strideE, offsetE,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    M,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL, offsetIFAIL
) → info: integer
```

Computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a real.
symmetric tridiagonal matrix A.

Eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be selected by specifying either a
range of values or a range of indices for the desired eigenvalues.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | 'no-vectors' or 'compute-vectors' |
| `range` | `"all" \| "value" \| "index"` | 'all', 'value', or 'index' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the tridiagonal matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Diagonal elements (length N), may be modified |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride for d |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for d |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length max(1, N - 1)</sub> | **in/out** · Subdiagonal elements (length N-1), may be modified |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride for e |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for e |
| `vl` | `number` | Lower bound of value interval (range='value') |
| `vu` | `number` | Upper bound of value interval (range='value')<br>Rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` |
| `il` | `integer` | 1-based index of smallest eigenvalue (range='index')<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max(1, N))` |
| `iu` | `integer` | 1-based index of largest eigenvalue (range='index')<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min(N, il) \|\| iu > N)` |
| `abstol` | `number` | Absolute error tolerance for eigenvalues |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output: number of eigenvalues found (M[0]) |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: selected eigenvalues in ascending order |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride for w |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for w |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)</sub> | **out** · Output: eigenvectors (if jobz='compute-vectors') |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of first dimension of Z |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of second dimension of Z |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for Z |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace (length >= 5\*N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for WORK |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * N</sub> | **out** · Integer workspace (length >= 5\*N) |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | Stride for IWORK |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for IWORK |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: indices of non-converged eigenvectors |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | Stride for IFAIL |
| ↳ `offsetIFAIL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for IFAIL |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found.
  -   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found.
  -   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found.
- `N`: The order of the matrix. $N \ge 0$.
- `d`: On entry, the n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix A. On exit, D may be multiplied by a constant factor chosen to avoid over/underflow in computing the eigenvalues.
- `e`: On entry, the (n-1) subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix A in elements 1 to N-1 of E. On exit, E may be multiplied by a constant factor chosen to avoid over/underflow in computing the eigenvalues.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.

  See "Computing Small Singular Values of Bidiagonal Matrices with Guaranteed High Relative Accuracy," by Demmel and Kahan, LAPACK Working Note #3.
- `M`: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.
- `w`: The first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. If an eigenvector fails to converge (`INFO` \> 0), then that column of Z contains the latest approximation to the eigenvector, and the index of the eigenvector is returned in `IFAIL`. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced. Note: the user must ensure that at least max(1,M) columns are supplied in the array Z; if `RANGE = 'V'`, the exact value of M is not known in advance and an upper bound must be used.
- `IFAIL`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M elements of `IFAIL` are zero. If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, then `IFAIL` contains the indices of the eigenvectors that failed to converge. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then `IFAIL` is not referenced.

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success, >0 if eigenvectors failed to converge

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, then i eigenvectors failed to converge. Their indices are stored in array `IFAIL`.

</section>

## Notes

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dstevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dstevx';

// Symmetric tridiagonal matrix with diagonal `d` and subdiagonal `e`:
const N = 3;
let d = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 4.0, 4.0 ] );
let e = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0 ] );
const M = new Int32Array( 1 );
const w = new Float64Array( N );
let Z = new Float64Array( N * N );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 5 * N );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 5 * N );
const IFAIL = new Int32Array( N );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = dstevx( 'column-major', 'compute-vectors', 'all', N, d, 1, e, 1, 0.0, 0.0, 1, N, 0.0, M, w, 1, Z, N, WORK, IWORK, IFAIL, 1 );
console.log( info, M[ 0 ], w, Z );

// Using the ndarray interface:
d = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 4.0, 4.0 ] );
e = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0 ] );
Z = new Float64Array( N * N );
info = dstevx.ndarray( 'compute-vectors', 'all', N, d, 1, 0, e, 1, 0, 0.0, 0.0, 1, N, 0.0, M, w, 1, 0, Z, 1, N, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0, IFAIL, 1, 0 );
console.log( info, M[ 0 ], w, Z );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSTEVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSTEVX computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a real symmetric tridiagonal matrix A. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be selected by specifying either a range of values or a range of indices for the desired eigenvalues.

</section>
